issues.situation: Knock-on through the support ledger. The fix bumps support_counts[obj] for the released screener before the later, non-screen leftovers run _find_best_remaining_objective (which subtracts committed x SUPPORT_STACK_PENALTY). At the finding itself (s7467 r1 P2), the designer reports this re-routes Kommandos A from obj_nml_2 to obj_center. The measured +3.64 does not include that move. Rollout overrides are applied per unit at execution (_take_rollout_override at AIDecisionMaker.gd:7004, after the plan is built), so branch B kept Kommandos A on obj_nml_2. The fix's actual plan is therefore an unmeasured two-unit change, and its only check is the designer's one-seed replay (-6 vs -13). Evidence on the knock-on move is mixed. Same matchup, round and player: s7468 r1 P2 Kommandos A to obj_center was harmful, -6.58 [-10.39, -2.78]. Other obj_center alternatives were also harmful (s7403 -11.08, s7423 r2 -12.00, s7408 -5.83, s7470 -5.50). But the AI's own support move to obj_center was the better option in s7417 r1 P2, s7418 and s7455.
issues.proposed_change: Do not bump support_counts for the released unit; drop the line `support_counts[svo_oid] = support_counts.get(svo_oid, 0) + 1`. Alternatively, apply the switch as a post-pass after the PASS 3 loop, so every other unit keeps its base assignment. The fix then reproduces the measured branch B exactly (Gretchin Advances to obj_nml_2, the rest unchanged).

issues.situation: The chosen trip is never vetted by the objective-pass gates. A leftover unit outside extra_obj_skipped / lone_skipped / far_skipped had every candidate 'covered' when visited. The PASS 2 loop `continue`s on remaining <= 0 (and on OBJ-ASSIGN-1's 'covered — falls through') before reprice/too_late/race_hopeless/lone_trip run. So 'nothing held it back' is vacuously true for svo_best in 100% of firings. TOO-LATE, RACE-SKIP and LONE-TRIP were never evaluated on the objective the fix sends the unit to.
issues.proposed_change: In the svo candidate loop, also skip candidates where `too_late.call(svo_cand) or race_hopeless.call(svo_cand) or lone_trip.call(svo_cand)`. These lambdas are in scope; the base LONE-TRIP support fallback in PASS 3 already calls lone_trip.call(s_cand).

issues.situation: 'Needs no fight' is not enforced. In _evaluate_all_objectives, 'uncontrolled' only means no OC is in range now; it is set from current OC with no proximity test, so it includes objectives the enemy is converging on. At the finding itself, the AI's chosen option read 'block Blade Champion Gamma approaching obj_nml_2 (16" away)'. 'held_safe' is also accepted, though the evidence has only one uncontrolled target. held_safe rarely clears screen + 8 anyway (WEIGHT_ALREADY_HELD_OBJ = -3).
issues.proposed_change: For the target, require `int(svo_eval.get("projected_enemy_oc", 0)) == 0`, i.e. no enemy can stand in range next move. The finding's obj_nml_2 passes this (Blade Champion 16" away, M6). Drop 'held_safe' from the state list.

issues.situation: Later-round secondary cost that a one-round rollout cannot see. The bench card pool includes Defend Stronghold: from R2, at the end of each opponent turn, +2 VP while no enemy unit is in your deployment zone, cumulative R2-R5. It also includes Outflank (3/5 VP for enemy units within 6" of a battlefield edge outside their territory) and Beacon (VP for the beacon unit outside its own deployment zone / territory). A deep striker that lands in the vacated backfield gap in R2 can deny or score these in R3-R5. The finding's E was measured only to the end of R2. Rare, because the fix fires at most once per movement phase, mostly in R1.
issues.proposed_change: Skip the switch when the AI holds Defend Stronghold, or when the opponent's active cards include Outflank or Beacon (the AI already tracks _secondary_awareness_pN). Or re-measure the finding with a 3-round horizon before shipping.

issues.situation: Validation coverage. The fix was checked at the finding plus six guardrails (in one-seed replays: 1 firing in 7 games). It was not checked at four other measured backfield-gap positions: s7472 r1 P1 1_1 Burna B (-1.58) and 2_2 Gretchin (-1.17), both with the alternative 'Move obj_home_1'; s7473 r1 P1 Gretchin (-0.08); s7474 r1 P1 Gretchin (+1.50). The session logs also show fix-eligible gap screens (no skip note) that were never measured: the s7408 sweep at R1 P2 (Burna Boyz A_P2 and B_P2) and the s7423 sweep at R2 P1 (Gretchin). The logged notes also differ from the report's labels: s7408 R1 P1 Burna A carries a RACE note, not LONE-TRIP. Either kind blocks the fix, so the gate outcome is unaffected.
issues.proposed_change: Run the same decision check at s7472 (both positions), s7473 and s7474. If it fires at the two s7472 positions toward obj_home_1, the state restriction in issue 3 (drop held_safe) is the natural guard.

issues.situation: Bench exposure; the shared premise is partly wrong. The denial branch is reached in the Custodes mirror. P2's Allarus Custodians are 16.2" from the nearest objective, so _evaluate_end_turn_redeploy picks the 'From Golden Light reposition' (>15", round <= 3) at the end of P1's R1 turn. That happened in 6/6 V9-era Custodes-mirror bench sessions (CHK / FIRETEST / FT2, 2026-10-30) and in 406/418 older-AI games. Strategic Reserves cannot arrive in round 1, so the unit is still IN_RESERVES during P1's R2 movement and re-enters by Rapid Ingress at the end of it. So P1's R2 plan does compute backfield gaps in nearly every Custodes-mirror game. This design still does not fire there: P1's only screening candidate is the 45-pt Prosecutors. In the V9-era bench games they were assigned in PASS 2 (capture obj_center). All 96 logged Custodes-mirror denial screens carried a skip note (72 are P1 R2 Prosecutors backfield gaps with RACE notes), so the gate blocks them.
issues.proposed_change: No change to this design. Do not widen the skip-set gate just to make the bench fire: it is the only thing separating the finding from the three negative-leaning gap guardrails. Report to the panel that this design will produce identical bench pairs, and that the Custodes-mirror P1 R2 gap screen exists if a bench-visible test is wanted.

issues.situation: Base-code context. _calculate_denial_positions samples the deployment zone's bounding box. On these maps the zones are triangles, so many 'backfield gap' points lie in no-man's land beside objectives. For P1 in s7472/s7473, (960,960) is about 6" from obj_center and (1600,960) about 6" from obj_nml_1. What the fix gives up is not always a low-value backfield spot.
issues.proposed_change: Out of scope for this fix. Optionally tag only samples that lie inside the real deployment-zone polygon as 'gap'; this would make the fix's premise (only low-value backfield spots are released) literally true.

reviews.fires_in_bench: About 0 (well under 1% of games) in all three fixtures; expect identical pairs, like V9's keeper fix. Orks mirror: no unit is ever IN_RESERVES at a movement phase. There is no From Golden Light-type redeploy, and the lead reports the Kult of Speed Orks never use Evasive Manoova, so the denial branch never runs. Asym (Custodes P1 vs Orks P2): the Orks never enter reserves, so P1 never runs the branch. P1's Allarus can only redeploy at the end of P2's turn and arrives in P1's next movement phase, before P2 moves. Custodes mirror: unlike the shared premise, the branch IS reached at P1's R2 movement in almost every game, because P2's Allarus uses From Golden Light (16.2" > 15") at the end of P1's R1 turn and cannot arrive in R1. That happened in 6/6 V9-era bench sessions and 406/418 older-AI games. But P1's only screening candidate is the Prosecutors (Custodian Guard is 215+ pts, Blade Champions are characters, split Allarus have OC 3 and ranged weapons). They are either assigned in PASS 2 (V9-era: capture obj_center) or carry a skip note (96/96 logged mirror denial screens), and the gate blocks them. P2 essentially never sees P1 reserves at its movement.
reviews.strengths: The narrowest possible change: one gated branch inside the PASS 3 denial step plus a 'gap' tag, no new scoring terms, and FIX_SCREEN_VS_OBJECTIVE = 0 restores base exactly. It reproduces the finding's alternative for the Gretchin (same unit, objective and Advance mode). The guardrails are respected by construction: screen-protect (the only harmful screen position, s7408 1_1, -5.83) and home-objective deep-strike denial are untouched. Units carrying any objective-pass skip are excluded, and the session logs confirm skip notes on the s7408 r1/r3 and s7423 r1 gap guardrails. Units standing on an objective (hold candidate) and plan-earmarked SCREEN units (which have no candidates) cannot be released. The plan is built once per movement phase (COORD-4), so the one-switch cap means at most one release per phase, except on re-plans. It does not depend on FIX_KEEPER_RELEASE and fits V9R. The failing-first test and the related test suites pass, per the report. The direction (more bodies forward) agrees with the round-2 lesson that held-back units score less on secondaries.
reviews.summary: The design is sound, very narrow and low-risk; I found no major game-impact problem. The trade-off is that it is almost inert. I estimate about 0 firings in all three bench fixtures, so the benchmark will show identical pairs and cannot confirm the +3.64 finding. One correction to the shared premise: the Custodes mirror does reach the denial branch at P1's R2 movement in nearly every game. P2's Allarus redeploys with From Golden Light at the end of P1's R1 turn and cannot arrive in round 1. This design is still blocked there, because P1's only screening candidate, the Prosecutors, is either assigned in PASS 2 or skip-flagged (96/96 logged mirror denial screens). In reserve-heavy games (the sweeps, human players) it fires at most once per phase, mostly in R1. The most useful revision is to drop the support_counts bump. Without it, the fix's plan equals the measured counterfactual. With it, at the finding it also re-routes Kommandos A to obj_center: an unmeasured move, and the same move was measured harmful for the same unit in s7468 r1 P2 (-6.58). Further hardening, all small: re-run too_late / race_hopeless / lone_trip on the chosen trip, which the gate never vetted; require projected_enemy_oc == 0 and drop held_safe, so 'no fight' is actually true; and keep the screen when Defend Stronghold, Outflank or Beacon makes backfield deep strikes costly in R3-R5, which a one-round rollout cannot see.

issues.situation: Test 2 (test_held_back_grots_keep_the_gap) asserts `action == "screen" or not reason.contains("not parked on a backfield gap")`. That assertion is true on base and true whenever the grots get any assignment other than this fix. On that board the boyz (20 OC) and grots (10 OC) can out-contest the enemy squad, so obj_mid probably reads enemy_weak with an open OC need, and the grots can get a pass-2 flip without ever reaching the gap branch (not run: I am read-only). No test covers the gates that actually separate the guardrails: extra_obj_skipped, lone_skipped and far_skipped, the hold-candidate exclusion, the one-switch-per-plan cap, and the home-objective denial exclusion. The test header claims LONE-TRIP, DIM-RETURNS and home-denial guardrails, but no test exercises them.
issues.proposed_change: Make test 2 assert the base outcome (action == 'screen' and reason begins with 'backfield gap') on a board where only the state filter can stop the switch. Example: 3 enemy OC1 models on obj_mid, so the boyz fully cover its need and the grots reach PASS 3 with no mark. Add these cases: (b) a far open objective (for example at y=40, about 7 turns at M5) gives the grots a TOO-LATE or LONE-TRIP mark, and they keep the gap with the fix on; (c) grots standing on a held objective keep the gap; (d) two spare screeners give exactly one switch; (e) when only a home-objective denial spot exists, there is no switch.

issues.situation: Evidence fidelity at the finding. (1) Drift: the case's live decision (signature pos:553,1472) was a corridor block, 'block Blade Champion Gamma approaching obj_nml_2'. The backfield-gap screen measured as branch A only appears because loading the mid-phase save rebuilds the plan over the units still movable (_turn_movement_plan is a static and is not saved). The fix only touches the gap branch, so in the original live plan it would most likely not have fired for the Gretchin. (2) Knock-on: in the replay the fix bumps support_counts, and this moves Kommandos A from obj_nml_2 to obj_center. The measured +3.64 used a ROLLOUT move override applied at execution time, after the plan was built, so Kommandos A stayed on obj_nml_2 in branch B. The fix's plan is therefore the measured alternative plus an unmeasured redirect (one seed only: -6 vs -13). The report says 'matches the alternative exactly' and does not mention the drift.
issues.proposed_change: Measure the fix itself at the finding: fix on vs fix off, the same 36 paired seeds. Or remove the `support_counts[svo_oid] = ... + 1` line so later support units keep their base plan, which makes the replayed plan equal branch B. State the drift in the report.

issues.situation: The released candidate never passes the trip gates. A covered objective's pass-2 candidate stops at `remaining <= 0`, so svo_best never goes through too_late, race_hopeless, lone_trip or far_trip. The 'uncontrolled' state also ignores enemy_nearby (only held_* uses it), so the comment's 'needs no fight' is not enforced. A late-round trip that arrives after round 5 can still clear the +8 margin. Example from a bench record: a 4-turn obj_nml_1 candidate scored 20.5 against a 6.5 gap screen.
issues.proposed_change: In the svo candidate loop add `if too_late.call(svo_cand) or race_hopeless.call(svo_cand) or lone_trip.call(svo_cand) or far_trip.call(svo_cand): continue`. The closures are in scope and cost a few calls per screener. Then re-run the s7467 replay to confirm the Gretchin still flips. Battlewagon A is assigned to obj_nml_2, so lone_trip should stay false.

issues.situation: The gate is broader than documented. `not extra_obj_skipped.has(unit_id)` blocks the release when any candidate of the unit got a DIM-RETURNS, TOO-LATE or RACE-SKIP mark, whatever objective it was for. A screener that falls through pass 2 normally visits a far open objective and gets a mark there. Example: in the V9 Custodes mirror, P1's round-2 Prosecutors carry 'not going for obj_home_2 - 5 turns away' (fire-test seed 96021). So the release fires almost only when every objective is already covered. The const comment lists only lone-trip, far-trip, race and diminishing-returns.
issues.proposed_change: Keep it, because it is the conservative side, but name TOO-LATE in the const comment and in the report. If more reach is wanted later, ignore TOO-LATE marks on objectives other than the target, and re-check the s7423 DIM-RETURNS guardrail when you do.

issues.situation: The report checks only the 6 cluster guardrails. measured_positions.json has 6 more backfield-gap screens with a move/advance alternative that this gate can reach: s7472 r1 P1 2_2, Gretchin gap vs Move obj_home_1, E -1.17 [-2.42, +0.08] (the screen is close to significantly better); s7472 r1 P1 1_1 -1.58; s7473 r1 P1 2_1 -0.08; s7474 r1 P1 2_0 +1.50; s7423 r1 P1 1_0 +0.33; s7408 r3 P1 2_7 +0.83. A seventh, s7436, has a Hold alternative and is excluded by the hold rule. Whether the fix fires at these positions, and where it sends the unit, is not reported.
issues.proposed_change: Replay at least s7472 2_2, s7472 1_1 and s7473 2_1 with the fix and add them to guardrail_checks: did it fire, and to which objective. If it fires toward obj_home_1 at s7472 2_2, remove held_safe home objectives from the release set.

issues.situation: Style and tuning. The margin reuses SCREEN_SCORE_BASE, which is also the first term of the screen score, so tuning it by delta moves the threshold by 2x delta. Raw scores of covered uncontrolled objectives (about 20 or more) still include the full capture value, although the unit's OC is not needed there. They clear screen + 8 almost always, so the margin mostly filters low-value held-objective reinforcements. Separately, the comment 'a unit standing on an objective is not released' is misleading: on base that unit still leaves its objective for the gap, and the condition only keeps the base choice.
issues.proposed_change: Use a dedicated param (for example SCREEN_VS_OBJ_MARGIN = 8.0). Reword the comment to say that such a unit keeps its base gap screen.

issues.situation: Shipping signal. The switch is nested in the same has_enemy_reserves denial branch as the other designs, so it fires about 0 times in the bench (see fires_in_bench). The side-swapped bench should therefore give identical pairs, as V9's keeper fix did (124/124). Widening the switch to the screen-protect or corridor-block branches would reach the bench, but there is no supporting evidence: s7408 screen-protect is -5.83 harmful, s7467 1_0 corridor block is -0.50, and s7435 is +0.11 with n=36.
issues.proposed_change: No code change for this narrow design. The ship decision must rest on the finding's rollouts plus the extra checks above (or on a bundle with a fix that does fire), not on a bench gain. Do not widen to the other screen branches without new measurements.

reviews.fires_in_bench:
About 0 firings; expect identical pairs. The switch only runs inside PASS 3's deep-strike-denial branch (has_enemy_reserves and is_screen_candidate, with a free denial spot), and additionally needs a gap spot, no skip mark, no hold candidate, and at most one switch per plan.

The bench is NOT reserve-free, so the premise 'every unit starts deployed' is incomplete. In the Custodes mirror, P2's Allarus Custodians are always moved to strategic reserves at the end of P1's round-1 turn (From Golden Light; V9 logs show '[SCORING] End-of-turn redeploy - moving U_ALLARUS_CUSTODIANS_A_P2 to reserves') and come back by Rapid Ingress at the end of P1's round-2 Movement phase. P1's round-2 plan therefore always runs the denial branch:
- In bench_data/ai_versions_2026-10-28 and ai_versions_11e_2026-10-29, 465 of 465 Custodes-mirror records show this redeploy.
- In 62 of them, P1's Prosecutors (the only Custodes screening candidate: 45 pts, OC2) screened a 'backfield gap' at round 2. That is the only round/player where denial screens ever appear.

Under the base AI (8f563d0 = 5e70bc2 with the keeper release off; 4 local fire-test games, seeds 96021 and 96031, both arms), P1's Prosecutors are already assigned by pass 2 or backfill at round 2 (to obj_center), so the branch is never reached. In seed 96021 they also carry a TOO-LATE mark (obj_home_2) that this gate excludes.

Later On Gilded Wings lifts are brought back in the owner's next Movement phase, so the opponent's planner never sees them. Only arm M2 (candidate plays P1) can fire in the Custodes mirror.

Orks mirror: 0. No unit ever enters reserves: the fixture's Deffkoptas lack Aerial Manoover, and the AI scores Kunnin' Infiltrator, Aerial Manoover, Da Jump and Shokk Attack Engine at 0.

Custodes vs Orks: about 0. Custodes P1 never sees Ork reserves, and the Ork planner would see Custodes reserves only if a lifted unit stayed off the table past the Custodes' own Movement phase.

Estimate: 0, at most a rare Custodes-mirror game.
reviews.strengths:
- The change is about as small as it can be: one gate in the PASS-3 denial branch plus a 'gap' tag in _calculate_denial_positions. With param 0 the game plays exactly as base: every new path sits behind a short-circuiting get_param >= 0.5; the tag is read only by the gate; _calculate_denial_positions has one caller; the only difference is a parameters_used entry in the decision record.
- No null or empty access problems. Candidate fields always exist, and an empty eval is checked before `.state`. Units with a SCREEN earmark have no candidates, so plan earmarks are still obeyed. Dead and reserve units never reach PASS 3. Ids and types match.
- The ledger stays consistent. The unit reuses its own candidate (same action, so Advance stays Advance), is labelled as a support assignment, support_counts is bumped once, and the denial index consumes the gap so later screeners keep their spots. Gap samples are 2R apart, so not adding the skipped gap to screener_positions changes nothing.
- The cost is negligible: one pass over the candidates per eligible gap screener until the first switch, and the plan is built once per phase.
- A new greppable [SCREEN_VS_OBJECTIVE] log line reports the scores, and no debug log is removed.
- The test pins the fix on and erases the override. It fails on base for the right reason: test 3 shows the base gap screen on the same board, and test 1 fails on it. It drives the real planner (_assign_units_to_objectives), not only a helper.
- The report's guardrail checks match the code's discriminators: screen-protect is out of scope, LONE-TRIP goes to lone_skipped, DIM-RETURNS goes to extra_obj_skipped, and home-denial spots have no gap tag. The designer also narrowed the gate after seeing a second, unwanted firing (Beast Snagga on obj_home_2).
- It does not depend on FIX_KEEPER_RELEASE, and its hunks do not overlap the lone_flip or reinforce_insurance finals.
reviews.summary:
The narrow patch is a clean, correctly gated change. In the PASS-3 deep-strike-denial branch, a screening unit that the objective passes did not mark (no extra/lone/far skip), that is not standing on an objective, and that is about to take a backfield-gap spot is instead sent to its best move/advance candidate on an uncontrolled or friendly-held objective, when that candidate scores at least screen + SCREEN_SCORE_BASE. There is at most one switch per plan. Param 0 plays exactly as base. I found no code bugs: no null access, no wrong ids, no double counting, no hot-loop cost, and no removed logs. The test proves the switch, fails on base for the right reason, and drives the real planner.

All issues are minor:
- The guardrail test is a weak OR assertion, and the gates that separate the guardrails are untested.
- The finding is a drift case. The live decision was a corridor block; the gap screen appears only when the plan is rebuilt from the mid-phase save. The fix's own plan also redirects Kommandos A through the support ledger, which was not measured.
- The chosen candidate never passes the too_late, race, lone-trip or far-trip gates, so 'needs no fight' is not enforced.
- The skip gate also catches TOO-LATE marks, which is not documented.
- Six other measured backfield-gap positions are unchecked, including s7472 r1 P1 2_2 at -1.17 [-2.42, +0.08].
- The margin is tied to SCREEN_SCORE_BASE.

Bench: the trigger is the same has_enemy_reserves branch as the other designs. The bench does contain enemy reserves: every Custodes-mirror game sends P2's Allarus to reserves before P1's round-2 move. But under V9 the only Custodes screener (Prosecutors) is already assigned before PASS 3 there, and it usually carries a TOO-LATE mark. Neither Ork side ever sees reserves. So expect about 0 firings and identical pairs. Any shipping evidence has to come from the rollouts, not from the bench.

issues.situation: The plan changes more than the measured decision. Situation: an Ork list with two or more units of 100 pts or less (Gretchin, Burna Boyz, Lootas, Beast Snagga Boyz) facing an army with reserves, rounds 1-3, with those units left for PASS 3. When SVO fires it `continue`s without `denial_idx += 1`. The next screening candidate (screeners are sorted first in PASS 3) then inherits the vacated gap and loses its base role (screen-protect, corridor-block or a later gap). Every later screener whose top option is the same capture is also redirected. The cap is checked against `support_counts` taken before the PASS-3 support fallback, and that fallback assigns the non-screen units only after all screeners. The plan is built once per movement phase (COORD-4), so nothing undoes this. The designer's own replays show it. At the finding s7467, the Beast Snagga Boyz also leave their screen for obj_nml_2 (unmeasured). obj_nml_2 then gets about 4-5 units in round 1 (Battlewagon Alpha, Mek and Kommandos per the report, plus Gretchin and BSB). The Gretchin passed the cap with '2 committed' only because the support-fallback units were not yet counted. At the harmful guardrail s7408 r1 P1, Burna Alpha leaves for obj_nml_1, which is unmeasured. Burna Beta is then moved off 'screening valuable friendlies' at (604,984), the action measured 5.83 VP better than its objective alternative, onto the vacated gap. At s7437 and s7423 the screeners' gap positions shift, though the report marks both 'changed: false'. In the measured branch B only the forced unit changed: the plan was stored, the Gretchin's gap stayed open and the BSB kept its base role.
issues.proposed_change: When SVO fires, also advance `denial_idx` (treat the gap as declined and leave it open, as in branch B), so later screeners keep their base assignments. Allow at most one SVO redirect per objective per plan, using a `svo_done[oid]` dictionary declared before the PASS-3 loop. Choose the redirected unit in a pre-pass as the cheapest eligible screener, so s7467 moves the Gretchin (45 pts) and not the BSB (80 pts). The plan then differs from the base by exactly the one unit that was measured. Add tests for the cascade and for two eligible screeners on one objective.

issues.situation: The 'uncontested' guard is missing for one-move trips. `race_lost` is computed only when `turns_to_reach > 1`. `lone_skipped` is filled only when PASS 2 evaluated the pair while OC was still needed, and that never happens for a capture whose OC need was already met, which is exactly the case SVO targets. `far_skipped` is always empty (FIX_FAR_TRIP=0). `planned_new_objs` includes flips of contested and enemy-held objectives (`apply_capture_assignment` adds every state except held_safe/held_threatened). So a fragile screener within one move of an objective the plan is flipping, or that enemies can reach next move, is redirected with no enemy check at all. Situation: rounds 2-3 while the enemy still has reserves, with Gretchin or Burna near the centre the plan is taking with 1-2 units. The designer's own s7423 replay sends Gretchin and Burna Beta to obj_center in round 2. That is the direction the measured screen positions point against: Burna to obj_center -5.83 (harmful, s7408), -3.25 (s7437), -2.83 (s7408).
issues.proposed_change: Replace the race_lost/lone_skipped guard with a direct test on the target's evaluation: `state == "uncontrolled"` and `enemy_oc == 0` and `projected_enemy_oc == 0`. This is the hint's 'needs no fight' test. The finding still passes: obj_nml_2's nearest Custodes unit is 16.4 in away, against the 13.8 in one-move reach (M8 + 2 + control range). Call `lone_trip.call(svo_cand)` (and `far_trip` when it is on) directly instead of reading `lone_skipped`/`far_skipped`. Add a test with a target one move away and an enemy unit within one move of it.

issues.situation: The bench cannot see this design, because it essentially never fires in the 3 fixtures (see fires_in_bench). The paired side-swapped bench will produce identical games, as with the keeper fix's 124/124. It can neither confirm the +3.64 nor catch a loss. The report's '0-4 fires per game' comes from sweep positions with deployment-time deep-strike reserves and the Orks_2000 list, not from the bench fixtures (post-deploy, Kult of Speed Orks, Lions Custodes).
issues.proposed_change: Do not count identical bench pairs as support. If the panel wants this design, validate it on a fixture with deployment-time deep-strike reserves, for example a pre-deploy Orks_2000 vs custodes_lions side-swapped pair, or park it until such a fixture exists.

issues.situation: The 'price' is decorative. svo_val is the candidate's full score (the whole objective value: about 20 at s7467, 26-39 for the Custodes Prosecutors in old records) minus 3.5 per committed unit (0-2). That always beats a gap screen (about 6.5-11), so eligibility alone decides. The unit's marginal value at an objective whose OC need is met (secondary actions, backup OC) is not modelled, although that is what the 'root' angle claims to fix. Across the 12 measured backfield-gap screens, the objective alternative averages about -0.4 VP (11 neutral, 1 clear). The evidence supports the filters, not a general 'objective beats gap'.
issues.proposed_change: Price the support from the unit's marginal terms only: its secondary_* score terms, plus backup OC when projected_enemy_oc > 0. Alternatively, require svo_val minus the screen score to exceed a margin calibrated on the measured positions. Otherwise, state plainly in the comment and report that this is an eligibility rule, not a re-pricing.

issues.situation: There is a later-round cost the measurement cannot see. reviews.summary: The root design is in effect a rule: a spare screener whose top option is a capture the plan already makes goes there instead of a backfield gap. It fixes s7467 and leaves the measured opposite positions alone. Four problems remain. (1) In the three bench fixtures it essentially never fires: Orks never enter reserves, Custodes reserves never overlap an Ork movement phase, and the single Custodes-mirror window (P1 round 2, Prosecutors) is taken by an earlier pass in V3-V5 and V9. The shipping bench will show identical pairs and can neither confirm nor refute it. (2) Where it does fire (Ork lists with several cheap units against armies with reserves), the plan changes more than the measured decision. The vacated gap passes to the next screener, and several screeners can go to the same objective. The designer's own replays show the BSB also leaving at s7467 (4-5 units on obj_nml_2 in round 1), and Burna Beta losing its screen-protect role at the harmful s7408 guardrail. (3) The 'uncontested' guard does not exist for one-move trips: race_lost is not computed, lone_skipped is never filled for covered objectives, and flips count as planned captures. Round 2-3 redirects to a contested centre are therefore possible (the s7423 replay). (4) The price comparison is decorative. Revise: advance denial_idx and allow one redirect per objective per plan (the cheapest eligible screener); require an uncontrolled target with enemy_oc == 0 and projected_enemy_oc == 0, plus a direct lone_trip check. In the case this fix targets, the objective's need is already met when the unit's candidate comes up, so pass 2 hits `remaining <= 0` and `continue`s before the LONE/FAR checks. issues.situation: The code never checks that the objective is uncontested. planned_new_objs also contains flips (enemy_weak, enemy_strong and contested states), and race_lost is only computed for trips of 2 or more turns. **Code: no major issue.** The change is clean and correctly gated, and param 0 restores V9 exactly. It merges cleanly onto V9R, and the test genuinely tests the fix. The minor issues are:
- The LONE-TRIP/FAR-TRIP exclusion never runs where the fix fires, because it reads skip dicts that pass 2 never fills for an already-covered objective.
- 'Uncontested' is never checked: flips and 1-turn trips under enemy threat qualify.
- planned_new_objs keeps stale entries, which allows a 'support' move with 0 units committed.

**Cautions for the panel:**
1. The single clear finding is not a real-game backfield-gap decision. The original game chose a corridor block at (553,1472). The gap at (1600,1520) appears only because the rollout rebuilds the plan from a mid-phase save. In the 11 measured positions where the real game chose a backfield gap, the alternatives average E ≈ -0.8. Kult of Speed's stratagems (Dakkastorm, Delicious Eating Squigs, Speediest Freeks) never remove units; the AI scores Aerial Manoover / Kunnin' Infiltrator / Da Jump at 0.0 (OrkAbilities11e ai value); no AIRCRAFT. Under V9 those lost-race trips mostly become LONE-TRIP skips, which also block this fix (lone_skipped check).

At the finding, the fix moves the Gretchin AND the Beast Snagga Boyz (OC 20) onto obj_nml_2, whose OC need was already met by Battlewagon/Mek/Kommandos. The measured branch B moved only the Gretchin (36 seeds); the fix's own decision at the finding has one replay seed (base -13, fix -10). screen_vs_obj_join ignores support_counts, so it bypasses the COORD-4 diminishing returns that make leftover units spread out; DIM-RETURNS/OVERCOMMIT do not price these joins either.

reviews.summary: The design is a sound, low-risk, narrowly guarded rule. It matches the one confirmed finding (s7467 r1 P2 Gretchin, +3.64 over 36 seeds), and its guards explain why the strongest opposite positions were left alone. I found no common full-game situation where it plays worse. Its decisive weakness for shipping is exposure: it needs the enemy to have units in reserve, and the three postdeploy bench fixtures almost never give that. The only bench window is P1's round-2 Movement in the Custodes mirror, where only the Prosecutors can be affected, so expect over 97% identical pairs. The bench can neither confirm nor reject it, and identical pairs must not be read as validation. Suggested narrowings: allow one join per objective per phase, so the fix's own decision at the finding matches the measured one (it currently also sends the Beast Snagga Boyz); fire only on gaps inside the zone while the 11e opponent-zone ban covers the enemy's next arrival (11 of 12 measured backfield-gap screens were in no man's land, only the finding was inside the zone); run the check after the spacing test; drop joins to already-held objectives; replay the 8 unchecked backfield-gap positions, including s7472. None of these changes alters the finding. issues.situation: The SVO block (patched AIDecisionMaker.gd ~10684) runs before the spacing check (too_close_to_screener ~10702-10708). Take a case where denial_positions[denial_idx] is a backfield gap within screen_spacing_px*0.5 (the denial radius) of a screener placed earlier in the same pass, typically a home-denial screener when home is empty. Base sends this unit, and every later screen candidate (denial_idx never advances), to SCREEN-PROTECT, CORRIDOR-BLOCK or support. The patch sends them forward instead. A qualifying objective is any objective in planned_new_objs or in state held_safe/held_threatened. planned_new_objs includes flips of enemy_weak, enemy_strong and contested objectives, so a 45-pt screen unit can be sent to join a fight. issues.situation: Cosmetic and minor efficiency points. race_hopeless.call(c) (patched line 10646) is dead code, because race_lost candidates are already skipped. The candidate list is sorted by score, so the loop could break at the first qualifying candidate. COORD-2's blocked_best loop (patched ~10889-10896) overwrites the SVO coordination_note when the unit joins a different objective than its blocked best one. None of these changes a decision.

reviews.fires_in_bench: About 0. Orks mirror: 0. No unit in the bench Ork list can enter reserves (no Da Jump, Kunnin' Infiltrator or Aerial Manoover, and Kult of Speed has no reserve stratagem), so has_enemy_reserves is never true. Custodes vs Orks (P1 Custodes, P2 Orks): 0. From Golden Light and On Gilded Wings both trigger at the end of the opponent's turn or Fight phase, and the AI brings the unit back in its own next Movement phase, so the Orks never see Custodes reserves in their own Movement phase. The Custodes never see Ork reserves. Custodes mirror: at most one window per game. It happens only in P1's round-2 Movement phase, after P2's From Golden Light at the end of P1's round-1 turn (reserves cannot arrive in round 1). The only eligible unit then is P1's 45-pt Prosecutors (every other Custodes unit costs more than 150 pts or is a CHARACTER). In both logged bench games (seeds 96021 and 96031, M1 and M2 logs) that window had 4-5 backfield-gap positions, but the Prosecutors were already assigned in pass 2. Expect roughly 0-0.1 fires per Custodes-mirror game and nearly all pairs identical, like V9's keeper fix (124/124).
reviews.strengths: Param 0 gives the base decisions exactly: the closure is never called, and the extra 'kind' key on denial positions is read only by the gated block. The trigger is narrow and reuses the planner's own guards: the extra_obj_skipped, lone_skipped and far_skipped early exit, plus too_late, lone_trip, far_trip and race_lost. It requires another unit already assigned to the objective or already moving there. Reading the code against the 5 cluster guardrails agrees with the report: units skipped by LONE-TRIP or DIM-RETURNS, home deep-strike denial and screen-protect positions are left alone. It uses apply_capture_assignment, so the OC ledger, planned_new_objs and reason text stay correct. It updates support_counts, explains the override in coordination_note, adds a distinct [SCREEN_VS_OBJECTIVE] log line and removes no debug log. I found no null-access, dead or reserve unit, wrong-id or double-count bug. Cost is one candidate scan per screen candidate facing a backfield gap, and only when enemy reserves exist. It does not depend on keeper release, and it applies cleanly on V9R (checked: git apply on 5e70bc2 plus keeper_release_rev_vs_v9.patch). The main test calls the real planner (_evaluate_all_objectives and _assign_units_to_objectives), sets the override at the start and erases it at the end, and fails on base for the right reason: the grots screen the backfield gap instead of joining.
reviews.summary:
The game design (/home/user/warhammer-40k-godot/tools/ai_lab/r4_designs/screen_vs_objective/game.patch in commit 07a4843, with its test 40k/tests/unit/test_ai_fix_screen_vs_objective.gd) is correct, cleanly gated and narrow. I found no major issue, so the verdict is ok.

In PASS 3, a screen candidate that is about to take a backfield-gap screen instead joins a forward objective, if all of these hold:
- No guard skipped the unit.
- The candidate is not race-lost.
- Its score is at least the screen score + 8.
- The plan is already taking or holding the objective, with another unit going there.

At s7467 this reproduces the measured Advance onto obj_nml_2. It also moves the Beast Snagga Boyz there; that second move was not measured.

Minor issues:
- The check runs before the spacing check. It can therefore take units that base would send to screen-protect or corridor-block, which the report says are untouched. Moving it inside `if not too_close_to_screener` fixes this.
- It allows joining flips of enemy-held objectives and reinforcing held ones, which is broader than the one uncontrolled-objective finding.
- Nothing limits how many units join one objective.
- Two guardrail sub-tests do not test what their names say: one never reaches the new code, and the LONE-TRIP one is blocked by RACE-SKIP first.

The point that matters most for shipping: the trigger needs enemy reserves, and the three bench fixtures declare none. The only mid-game source in these lists is the Custodes Allarus repositioning, and only P1 in the Custodes mirror ever sees it (round 2). By then the only eligible unit, the Prosecutors, was already assigned in both logged bench games. Expect about 0 fires and identical pairs. The bench cannot show a gain, so shipping would rest on one 36-seed position.

I did not run Godot (the repo was read-only for this review). The fire estimate comes from the fixture saves, the code's trigger conditions and the two logged Custodes-mirror bench games.

scores.note: Flips s7467 to the measured alternative: the same unit, obj_nml_2 and Advance mode. It did not fire in any of the 6 guardrail replays, so the harmful s7408 1_1 screen-protect is untouched. The test fails on base (3 pass, 1 fail) and passes on the fix. Param 0 restores V9 exactly. The block sits inside the too_close_to_screener check and consumes the gap with denial_idx += 1, so there is no cascade to the next screener, and there is at most one switch per plan. Weaknesses: (1) It bumps support_counts, so Kommandos A is re-routed from obj_nml_2 to obj_center. That move is unmeasured, and the fix's plan is therefore not branch B. It also does not append the gap to screener_positions. (2) The released trip is never checked. PASS 2 skips covered objectives before TOO-LATE, RACE-SKIP and LONE-TRIP run, and the COORD-4 backfill refuses a unit without leaving a skip mark. (3) It accepts held_safe, held_threatened and home targets, and has no projected_enemy_oc check. (4) The margin reuses SCREEN_SCORE_BASE. (5) The guard test is a weak OR assertion. (6) The hold-candidate rule and the one-per-plan cap were added to fit s7467. Bench: about 0 fires, because no postdeploy fixture has reserves when the planner runs.

Flips s7467 to Advance obj_nml_2. It has the best guard set: skip marks and race_lost block it, it re-runs too_late, race_hopeless, lone_trip and far_trip on the chosen trip, it only joins units already there, and it excludes home. The test fails on base (9 pass, 3 fail). However: (1) It also sends Beast Snagga Boyz to obj_nml_2, an unmeasured 2-unit change. (2) At s7423 round 2 it sent two units to obj_center, the direction the measured screens favour against. (3) It has no stacking cap. (4) It does not advance denial_idx, so later screeners cascade. (5) The SVO block runs before the too_close_to_screener check, so it can divert units that base sends to screen-protect or corridor-block, the class of the harmful s7408 1_1 guardrail. (6) planned_new_objs lets it join flips of enemy-held objectives. (7) Two guard sub-tests never reach the new code, and race_hopeless is dead code. (8) The s7438 guardrail is not reported. Bench: about 0 fires.

Cannot win. It flips s7467 but also moves Beast Snagga Boyz, and it fired in 5 of 7 replays, changing measured guardrail units. At the harmful s7408 1_1, Burna Alpha leaves for obj_nml_1. Burna Beta then inherits the vacated gap: it leaves its measured-better screen-protect at (604,984) for (960,960), 6.3" from obj_center, 2.5" closer to the harmful alternative's objective. Other problems: (1) No denial_idx advance, so later screeners cascade. (2) The lone and far checks read skip dicts that are never filled for covered objectives, so they never trigger. (3) No extra_obj_skipped gate. (4) 'Uncontested' is never checked: flips and one-turn trips under threat qualify. (5) The 'price' (full score minus 3.5 per committed unit) always beats the 6-11 point screen once a unit is eligible, so the comparison is decorative. (6) The test has a single objective, and its race test passes on base. Bench: about 0 fires.

verdict.reasons:
Narrow wins, but I recommend PARKING it, because the bench cannot measure it.

All three designs reproduce the measured alternative at the finding: the Gretchin Advances onto obj_nml_2. All three are param-gated with param 0 equal to V9. All three apply cleanly to 5e70bc2 and to 5e70bc2 + keeper_release_rev_vs_v9.patch; I checked this with git apply --check on scratch copies. None depends on FIX_KEEPER_RELEASE. Each has a test that fails on base and drives the real _evaluate_all_objectives + _assign_units_to_objectives path.

Why narrow wins:
- Its plan is the closest to the measured branch B: one unit changes, the gap is consumed, the block sits inside the spacing check, and there is at most one switch per plan.
- It fired in none of the 6 guardrail replays.
- Its gaps (unchecked trip, target states broader than the evidence, the support-ledger knock-on) are cheap filter and bookkeeping edits.

Game has the best guards but structural side effects: it moves 2 units at the finding, cascades later screeners, can override screen-protect because it runs before the spacing check, and has no cap.

Root is the broadest design, and it moved the harmful guardrail's unit, so it cannot win.

Why park (verified):
- Every unit in mirror_custodes_2000, mirror_orks_2000 and asym_2000_postdeploy starts DEPLOYED, and none is in reserve. The bench Ork list has no way to enter reserves.
- The only window is the Custodes mirror at P1 round 2. In the V9 check game (/tmp/v9check, seed 96021, both arms), P1's Prosecutors are assigned at round 2 by the COORD-4 backfill (moving to flip obj_center), so PASS 3 is never reached.
- So expect identical pairs. A design that only produces identical pairs cannot meet pooled bench E > 0.

Evidence caveats:
1. The finding's live decision was a corridor block at (553,1472). The backfield gap at (1600,1520) appears only because the rollout rebuilds the plan from a mid-phase save (_turn_movement_plan is not saved). Its real-game frequency is unknown.
2. The other 11 measured positions whose live choice was a backfield gap average about E -0.76 for the objective alternative, and none is significant.
3. 11 of the 12 measured gap screens are bounding-box samples in no-man's land on the diagonal map (checked for s7408, s7467 and s7472). Only the finding's gap is inside the zone.
4. In this engine, ingress_opponent_dz_ban_applies() exempts Deep Strike. Deep strikers can therefore land in our zone from round 2, so a vacated gap has a real cost in rounds 2-3. The round-2 lesson (units held back lose secondary VP) supports pushing units forward, but nothing after round 2 is measured.

Score totals are the sum of the five criteria (0-50).
required_changes: PARK: in any V10 merge, set `const FIX_SCREEN_VS_OBJECTIVE: float = 0.0`, or leave the patch out of V10. The bench gives identical pairs, so it cannot meet pooled bench E > 0. Enable it only after the reserve-carrying full-game A/B in extra_checks shows E > 0.

Reproduce branch B exactly: in the switch block, delete `support_counts[svo_oid] = support_counts.get(svo_oid, 0) + 1` and add `screener_positions.append(denial_pos)` next to `denial_idx += 1`. Every later screener and support unit then keeps its base assignment. At s7467, Kommandos A stays on obj_nml_2, as in branch B, instead of the unmeasured re-route to obj_center.

Check the released trip: in the svo candidate loop, `continue` when `svo_cand.get("race_lost", false) or too_late.call(svo_cand) or race_hopeless.call(svo_cand) or lone_trip.call(svo_cand) or far_trip.call(svo_cand)`. PASS 2 `continue`s on covered objectives before these gates, and the COORD-4 backfill refuses a unit without recording a skip mark, so today the chosen trip is never checked. The game design applies these same gates at s7467 and still flips the Gretchin.

Narrow the target to the evidence. Accept only `svo_eval.state == "uncontrolled"`, `int(svo_eval.get("projected_enemy_oc", 0)) == 0` and `not svo_eval.get("is_home", false)`, which drops held_safe, held_threatened and home targets. Also require `int(support_counts.get(svo_oid, 0)) >= 1`, so the unit always joins a unit that actually holds the objective or is going there; this also blocks a stale planned capture whose taker converted to an attack. obj_nml_2 passes all of these: it is uncontrolled, in no-man's land, the nearest enemy (Blade Champion Gamma) is 16.4" away against a 13.8" one-move reach, and per the designers Battlewagon Alpha is assigned there.

Add `const SCREEN_VS_OBJECTIVE_MIN_GAIN: float = 8.0`, read with get_param, for the margin instead of reusing SCREEN_SCORE_BASE, which is also the first term of the screen score. In the const comment, name TOO-LATE among the blocking marks, and say that a unit standing on an objective keeps its base gap screen.

Tests: in test_held_back_grots_keep_the_gap, replace the OR assertion with the exact base outcome (action == "screen" and reason begins with "backfield gap"), on a board where only the new target filter blocks the switch (for example, an enemy within M+2" plus control range of obj_mid). Add one case per gate, each failing when its gate is removed: (a) a LONE-TRIP or TOO-LATE mark keeps the gap; (b) a unit on an objective keeps the gap; (c) two spare screeners give exactly one switch; (d) with only a home-denial spot there is no switch; (e) a non-screen support unit gets the same objective with the fix on and off. Run on V9R: the tests must fail on base and pass on the fix.
grafts: From game: set a coordination_note on the released unit, for example 'not screening the backfield gap at (x,y), joining <units> at <obj>', so the decision card explains the override. The narrow patch only appends text to the reason.

From the game reviews, with the premise corrected: tag each gap `in_zone` using Geometry2D.is_point_in_polygon against our real deployment-zone polygon (treat the fallback rectangle as in-zone), and release units only from in-zone gaps. On the diagonal crucible_of_battle map, the bounding-box sampler puts 3 of 6 P1 samples in no-man's land 6-11" from objectives. 11 of the 12 measured gap screens were such points, and they lean toward keeping the screen. The finding's (1600,1520) is the only in-zone gap. Do NOT add the proposed round gate: GameState.ingress_opponent_dz_ban_applies() exempts Deep Strike, so enemy deep strikers can land in our zone from round 2.

From the root review: when several screeners qualify, release the cheapest unit without ranged weapons first, chosen in a pre-pass, instead of the first eligible unit in the unstable PASS-3 sort order. This stops a Lootas-type shooter from giving up its shooting.

Optional, only if the 3-round horizon check shows a late cost: keep the gap screen when our active secondaries pay for an empty home zone (a Defend Stronghold-type card, read via _secondary_awareness_pN).
extra_checks: Decision check on V9R (FIX_KEEPER_RELEASE OFF) at s7467_r1_p2_movement_2. Base must still screen the gap at (1600,1520). The revised fix must log exactly one [SCREEN_VS_OBJECTIVE] line (Gretchin -> ADVANCE obj_nml_2), and every other unit's assignment must match base (diff the plan block).

Measure the fix itself at s7467: fix on vs fix off, not a forced override, over the same 36 paired seeds. Expect about +3.6 with a CI above 0. Repeat with the horizon extended to the end of round 3: P1 holds 715 pts of deep-strike reserves (Allarus, Blade Champion A, Custodian Guard D), and deep strike may land in P2's zone from round 2.
Replay from the phase-start save s7467_r1_p2_movement_1, where the live choice was a corridor block. Report whether the fix fires in the real phase plan, and for which unit.

Fire/no-fire replays at every other measured screen position: s7408 r1 P1 1_1 (harmful) and 2_2, s7408 r3 P1 2_7, s7423 r1 P1 1_0 and 2_1, s7436 r1 P1 2_0, s7437 r1 P2 2_3, s7469 r1 P2 2_0, s7472 r1 P1 1_1 and 2_2, s7473 r1 P1 2_1, s7474 r1 P1 2_0, s7451, s7456, s7438. It must not fire at s7408 1_1, s7408 2_2, s7437, s7423 2_1 or s7472 (all lean toward the screen). Measure any other fire with at least 12 seeds.

Bench smoke: run the 3-fixture side-swapped bench with the fix ON and AI_LAB_KEEP_LOG_GREP='[SCREEN_VS_OBJECTIVE]'. Confirm 0 fires and identical pairs; any pair that differs must trace to a logged fire.
Param 0: confirm byte-identical decision records vs V9R on 2 or more seeds, on one bench fixture and on one reserve-carrying fixture.

Before un-parking: run a paired, side-swapped full-game A/B (24 or more pairs) on a fixture with deployment-time Deep Strike and Strategic Reserves, for example the custodes_lions vs Orks_2000 sweep lists, with Orks in both seats. Report rounds 3-5 and secondary-card VP separately (the round-2 lesson).
Run the new test (it must fail on base and pass on the fix) and the 18 related suites the designer listed, on V9R.
verdict.merge_risk: Code risk is low, and the bench cannot measure the behaviour. The change is one param-gated branch in PASS 3 plus a tag in _calculate_denial_positions. It applies cleanly to 5e70bc2 and to 5e70bc2 + keeper_release_rev_vs_v9.patch (checked with git apply --check on scratch copies). It does not depend on FIX_KEEPER_RELEASE, and param 0 equals V9R. It fires only when the enemy has units in reserve during our movement phase, so the postdeploy bench shows identical pairs and can neither confirm nor refute the +3.64. Where it does fire (reserve-heavy sweep or human games, mostly rounds 1-2), at most one cheap unit per movement plan leaves a backfield gap. In this engine, enemy deep strikers can land in that zone from round 2. Rounds 3-5 and Defend Stronghold-type secondaries are unmeasured. Keep it parked (const 0.0) until a reserve-carrying full-game A/B is run.
